Subject: Enablement & econ ops: implementation sprint and tuning checklist

Hi Ava — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to pull together the pragmatic plan for the first two-week implementation sprint that focuses on cost/perf wins (batching, cache, quant profiles, and routing).

Attached is a working "Econ Tuning Matrix" (econ_tuning_matrix_v1.xlsx) that maps variants we'll try in the pilot with target SLOs and success criteria. High-level asks:
- Confirm traffic slice for the pilot (estimated qps and typical seq lengths)
- Provide network diagram or IP allowlist details if you want private deployment (attached stub is fine)
- Agree on measurement windows and ownership for token-level cost reporting

Proposed schedule (2 weeks):
1) Day 0-2: onboarding, credentials, baseline perf capture
2) Day 3-6: batching + KV cache experiments (prefix caching for repeating prompts)
3) Day 7-10: quant profile A/B tests (fp16, q4_0, q3_k9)
4) Day 11-14: routing policies & fallback rules, finalize rollouts

If that looks good I'll slot Monica as the CS lead and Marissa as the econ ops owner for measurements. Can you confirm a pilot start date next week and who on your side will own logs/metrics access?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Rafael — this looks great, thanks for the clear plan. Quick answers:
- Pilot traffic: ~25 QPS peak, median seq length ~220 tokens, 90th pct around 540 tokens. We can carve a 10% user traffic slice for the pilot.
- Network: attaching our network diagram (included in your email) and we'll share the allowlist details once we confirm the start date.
- Metrics: Ben will own logs and can push infra access to your team; he prefers using the S3 delivery for raw traces + Grafana dashboard for aggregated metrics.

We can start Monday 20 Sep. Ben and I will be available for a 30m kickoff that morning. Can you make 09:30 PT?

Best,
Ava Richards

Rafael — draft attached: Econ runbook excerpt and two quant profiles I recommend for the pilot:
- conservative-q4: q4_0 with activation compression; expected throughput +30%, minimal quality drop (used for high-value short prompts)
- aggressive-q3: q3_k9 with per-layer calibration; expected throughput +70% but increased risk at tail; use behind A/B routing and gated to <10% traffic until validated

Also included notes on batching window recommendations (15ms for low-latency slice, 60ms for batch-throughput runs) and a KV cache approach (prefix TTL 5m, cold-cache warming during off-peak).

I'll join Monday's kickoff and bring the tuning matrix.
